question: In ancient times, the area to the south of the Ganga was known as ______.
solution:
The correct answer is Magadha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The region south of the **Ganga** along these rivers was referred to as **Magadha** in the past. Its kings established a sizable realm and were extremely strong. There were also established kingdoms in other regions of the nation. 
 
• Before **Bihar** was expanded, **Magadha** was a **territory** and **one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas, or "Great Kingdoms,**" of the **Second Urbanization**, which occurred at the **eastern Ganges Plain between 600 and 200 BCE.**
 
• The **Ganga, Sone, and Champa rivers**, in that order, confined the original **Magadha kingdom's territory** to the north, west, and east, while the eastern spurs of the **Vindhya** **mountains** formed its southern border.

 [IMAGE: https://i.pinimg.com/474x/62/91/57/62915799c2928c33d102afa5774d9b04.jpg] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ganga**

 
 
• A **transnational river in Asia**, the **Ganges** passes through **Bangladesh and India**.
 
• The 2,704 km river has its source in the **Uttarakhand** region of **India's western Himalayas**.
 
• It receives the **Yamuna**, a **right-bank tributary** that rises in the **western Indian Mountains**, as well as many left-bank tributaries from **Nepal**, which account for the majority of its flow, as it runs south and east across the **Gangetic plain of North India.**
 
• **Rivers flow into the Ganga from both banks**. The **Yamuna and Son** are its tributaries on its right bank. While some left bank tributaries include the **Gomti, Ghaghara, Gandak, and Kosi.**
 
• It is **India's largest river system.**
